newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move higher in early morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks moved higher at the open on Tuesday morning, prompted by optimism following Wall Street's overnight rebound but remaining guarded on the market's near term outlook, brokers said.
"We are locked in a trading range with the risk still slightly to the downside," said Chris Geiger, associate director, Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index was trading 60 points higher at 12,356 after rising to an early session high of 12,379.67. Turnover in the first 30 minutes was a robust HK$1.16 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 60.21 points, or 0.94 percent, to 6,451 following reports of better-than- expected corporate earnings on Monday.
The benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, however, ended slightly lower at 93-10/32, down 1/32, to yield 7.17 percent, in cautious trade.
In the near term the higher interest rate outlook is affecting sentiment and market liquidity, said Geiger.
"Liquidity from overseas is needed to lift this market and for the moment with interest rates in the States headed higher, it doesn't look like that money is going to be coming in," he added.
Finance issues and mid caps led the market up.
Index heavyweight HSBC Holdings regained HK$2.50 to HK$183.00, following Monday's HK$3.50 fall.
"The share has limited upside," said one broker with a large British house. "But it will be pushed up by index arbitraging."
Hang Seng Bank gained HK$1.25 to HK$81.00 and Bank of East Asia added HK$0.15 to HK$26.15.
Red chips were also sought. Leading the mid cap 50 index was red chip China Resources with a jump of HK$1.10 to HK$19.50.
Shanghai Industrial soared HK$1.70 to HK$40.80 on robust turnover of HK$134.93 million.
The share is reflecting a 37 percent upgrade in the company's earnings outlook following the injection of new assets, Geiger said.
New World Development led the losers with a fall of HK$0.50 to HK$39.30 but on thin trade of only HK$26.47 million.
April Hang Seng futures were a 100 points higher at 12,325, but were still trading at a discount to the cash market.
